notes: Summary: Aerolith builds a digital-first contact center platform used by e-comm and travel verticals (500–700 agents).
Primary ask: Agent assist with high-precision citations (must show source + timestamp) and ticket summarization that preserves links to original KB entries.

RAG specifics discussed: must support multi-source retrieval (Zendesk articles, Confluence KB, product release notes in S3). Freshness requirement: index updates every 2 hours for release notes, nightly for KBs; ability to mark ephemeral docs with TTL.
Search requirements: hybrid retrieval (BM25 + dense) with configurable recall/precision tradeoff per route. Need reranker option and per-query citation list limited to top 5 sources.

Latency/throughput: agent-assist end-to-end generation SLO 600ms p95 under normal load (200 concurrent agents); spike tolerance to 1,200 concurrent agents with graceful degradation (cached or short-form answers). Retrieval-only calls should be <120ms p95.
Reliability: must support automatic fallback to cached answers + simpler model family during infra pressure. Explicit canary + A/B rollout for model changes required.
Model preferences: prefer quantized open LLM for day-to-day; allow burst to higher-capacity commercial model for escalations (audit trail required).

Privacy/compliance: data residency for EU accounts, KMS for envelope encryption, and full audit trail for every model call (token level). Sec team asked: can Redwood provide per-request logging + redaction hooks?

POC scope: Ingest connectors (Zendesk/Confluence/S3) -> build vector index with metadata (doc source, last_updated) -> RAG stack providing citations and confidence score -> agent UI widget w/ tool-calls (create ticket, escalate).
Quote from Head of Support (A. Ruiz): 'We need answers our agents trust — citations are non-negotiable. If the model hallucinates, that's worse than no answer.'

SE notes (Priya): Focus on chunking strategy (semantic chunks around 250-700 tokens), metadata filtering, and TTL tags on release notes. Evaluate Redwood's automatic prefix caching and batch KV-cache behavior for repeated conversational context.
Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to pay for reliability/SLAs but wants Optimize recommendations to reduce token/unit cost (suggested batching & cache templates).
Integration notes: must support SSO (SAML), SCIM for provisioning, and webhook for ticket actions.
